title: Adding PLDM dissector for BIOS Specification
description:
This commit implemements PLDM dissector for the BIOS specification of the protocol which is done following DMTF guideline documentation- https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0247_1.0.0.pdf

Testing : For verification of dissector pcap file collected during host poweron is used as well as used custom pcaps.

Signed-off-by: Riya Dixit riyadixitagra@gmail.com

Use `wmem_strbuf_finalize` here instead of `wmem_strbuf_get_str` will free up the stuff internal to `version_buf` (which is no longer needed/used anyway) and will give you back just the string.

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19058/diffs?diff_id=1279732077&start_sha=2eb5bc9d18ae8098e334c705365fb0db67f32494#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_677_677)
We're switching away from these GLib types to standard C/C99 types.  Please use `uint16_t` instead of `guint16` here and throughout the rest of your change.

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19058/diffs?diff_id=1279732077&start_sha=2eb5bc9d18ae8098e334c705365fb0db67f32494#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_1359_1359)

The convention in the rest of this file (and throughout much of the Wireshark codebase) is to put a space after **each C keyword**.  Could you please do a quick search-and-replace to clean up all instances of these:

`if(` -> `if (`

`switch(` -> `switch (`

`for(` -> `for (`

`}else` -> `} else`

`else{` -> `else {`

Also a space around operators would improve readability and improve consistency with the rest of the file as well, i.e. `rem_bytes-4` -> `rem_bytes - 4` on this line, `rem_bytes%4` -> `rem_bytes % 4` on line 1382, and so forth.

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19058/diffs?diff_id=1279732077&start_sha=2eb5bc9d18ae8098e334c705365fb0db67f32494#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_1369_1369)
This function can be `static` unless you intend to use it from some other dissector.
`static` for this one too?  And so on throughout the rest of the functions added in this change.
`bios` -> `BIOS`

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19058/diffs?diff_id=1279732077&start_sha=2eb5bc9d18ae8098e334c705365fb0db67f32494#3a08d2566372818bf849b51bed343c98e42ff89b_1920_1920)

The aim here is clearly to pass the request's `table_type` to the dissection of the response, but this is not the way to do it.  Packets can be dissected out-of-order (e.g. scrolling around in the Wireshark UI) or there might be two simultaneous PLDM streams being dissected and the packets interleave such that one conversation's request interferes with the other's response.

Consider referring to `doc/README.request_response_tracking` in your Wireshark tree to learn how to handle this correctly.

Although what you have here is not the best approach, I won't object if you choose to defer fixing this and leave it as-is for now.  It should work sort-of sufficiently in the most common cases (sequential dissection, and only one PLDM stream at a time)... but it will definitely need to be fixed up in due course.
It's very simple, statics are not allowed. We're not going to accept maintenance responsibility for this, this has to be resolved.
It would be nice to have some `enum` or `#define` to use here (and in similar places) instead of just the bare numbers.
`return;` at the end of a function returning `void` is of no use.  Remove it?  Same comment for several more functions added in this commit.

Discussion in Discord `#developer-den` says that the use of `return;` at the end of a function returning `void` is really a stylistic choice; The way you have it now is fine if that is what you prefer. :slight_smile:
Rather than zeroing `str_len` at the end of the loop, can you move its declaration to line 1364 so that is within the loop scope and initialized there?

I thought that the loop structure and choice of variables here were a bit unusual... until I found it in the PLDM specification.

Might be worth adding a brief comment somewhere just above the loop to explain:

   `Padding algorithm as described in DSP0247 ver 1.0.0 section 7.1.`

or similar.

(My _personal_ choice would have been to calculate the net change in `*offset` instead of separately updating `L` for each step, but I can also see how there is some value in plainly implementing the same algorithm as in the specification.)
Should this really be inside `if (num_pad_bytes > 0)`?  That does not look correct to me.

I do not understand why this is needed.  Unless I misunderstand something here, this is part of the "transmit" side algorithm, not the "receive" side, and the assignment two lines earlier has already computed the correct number of pad bytes the receiver should expect, hasn't it?

I also do not understand why GitLab shows so much context here without making clear that this thread is related **only** to line 1384.  (Likewise for some of my other feedback where the context is unclear... it's usually just for the last line of context.)

Hi @riyadixitagra!

My review is taking some time, so I figured I would send you one "instalment" of feedback and I will continue reviewing tomorrow.  I hope that is OK.

Let me know if you have any concerns about my feedback.  Thanks!
